landingWelcome.title: Explore conservation planning options for Colombia.
landingWelcome.description: This decision-support tool helps compare precomputed conservation solutions across Colombia. Use it to see how different biodiversity targets, included areas, and cost assumptions change the places highlighted for conservation action.
landingWelcome.decisionSupportNote: The solutions are intended to inform discussion and planning; they do not replace local expertise, policy review, or final conservation decisions.

modal.title: Conservation feature breakdown

modal.additionalDescription: This domain was measured but was not targeted by the prioritization. The 17% and 30% values are illustrative range-coverage checkpoints, not user targets or performance benchmarks.
modal.strategicRasterAdditionalDescription: These are post-hoc, raster-derived Additional Outcomes, not solver targets. Each percentage divides solution-covered feature area by the authoritative aligned value-1 area for that strategic ecosystem; 17% and 30% are illustrative checkpoints.

modal.ecosystemTargetedDescription: These classification views describe the same national MEC ecosystem map. Pre-existing and new solution coverage are area shares; total coverage is compared with the configured target. Coarser classifications are area-based coverage rollups, not separate Prioritizr feature records.
modal.ecosystemAdditionalDescription: These classification views describe the same national MEC ecosystem map. Pre-existing and new solution coverage are area shares; total coverage is compared with the illustrative 17% and 30% checkpoints. Coarser classifications are area-based coverage rollups, not separate Prioritizr feature records.

step1.targetTypeIntro: Select one or more target groups for what to protect. For each selected target, choose a coverage level (17% or 30%).
step1.ecosystemsHelp: Uses detailed biome-region classes from Colombia’s official MEC 2024 ecosystem data. A 17% or 30% coverage level means the solution tries to represent that share of each of 429 detailed Humboldt/IAvH classes, such as “Hidrobioma Alto Caquetá”; the left sidebar groups those classes into 8 broad biome families so the map stays readable.
step1.speciesRichnessHelp: Prioritizes individual Humboldt BioModelos species layers for mammals, birds, amphibians, reptiles, and plants, covering many of the 8,751 species represented in Humboldt biomodels. Freshwater fish are not considered because the available fish species data is too coarse for this prioritization.
step1.speciesNationalResponsibilityHelp: Each species uses its own configured target.
step1.strategicEcosystemsHelp: Uses four strategic ecosystem input layers: páramos, wetlands, and tropical dry forest from Minambiente/SIAC, plus mangroves from INVEMAR. A 17% or 30% coverage level means the solution tries to include that share of each strategic ecosystem layer.
step1.ecosystemServicesHelp: Targets the two ecosystem-service features represented in this release: freshwater regulation and carbon storage.
step1.targetLevelRequiredHint: Select one or more target types. Each selected target also needs a coverage level (17% or 30%) before Step 2 unlocks.
step1.selectLevelToContinue: Select 17% or 30% to complete this target.
step1.summarySelectTarget: Select one or more target types to continue.
step1.summaryNeedsLevel: {{selected}} selected · {{remaining}} still need a coverage level.
step1.lockReasonSelectTargetType: Choose at least one target type to continue.
step1.lockReasonSelectTargetLevel: Choose 17% or 30% for each selected target type.
step1.targetLevelIntro: National representation goal as a percent target (17% or 30%).
step1.targetLevelRationale: The 17% option follows Aichi Biodiversity Target 11 for terrestrial and inland water conservation by 2020. The 30% option follows Target 3 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, which calls for conserving at least 30% of land, inland waters, and coastal and marine areas by 2030.
step1.strategicLevelFixed: 30% — only level available for strategic ecosystems in the current catalog.

step2a.includeOmecsHelp: OMECs are areas outside formal protected areas that are recognized for delivering conservation outcomes. Turn this on if the scenario should treat OMECs as already included coverage.
step2a.includeComunidadesLabel: Include Community Councils for Black Communities
step2a.includeComunidadesHelp: Turn this on if the scenario should treat legally recognized Community Councils for Black Communities as already included coverage.
step2a.includeResguardosHelp: Turn this on if the scenario should treat legally recognized Indigenous reserve territories as already included coverage.
step2a.alwaysRunapHelp: RUNAP is Colombia's National System of Protected Areas. These areas are always treated as already included coverage, so matching solutions focus on additional priority areas outside them.

step2b.intro: Choose a cost layer to evaluate potential conservation areas.
step2b.humanFootprintHelp: Shows where human activities have had a stronger or weaker impact on Colombia's landscapes.
step2b.humanFootprintDefinition: In this search, human footprint is used as a cost or trade-off layer. Higher values generally mean greater human pressure from land use, infrastructure, long-term intervention, or ecosystem vulnerability. It is a pressure signal, not a complete measure of ecological condition by itself.
step2b.carbonOpportunityHelp: Shows potential agricultural net benefit; higher values indicate a higher opportunity cost for conservation.
step2b.carbonOpportunityDefinition: Agricultural rent estimates the income, profit, or rental value that land could generate from productive uses such as agriculture, livestock, forestry, or fishing. It is used here as a cost layer: higher values suggest places where conservation could require giving up more potential agricultural benefit.

This is the SIRAP boundaries layer, so the Spanish source term "límites" refers to the boundary lines shown on the map. The combined layer includes territorial SIRAP boundaries plus thematic additions such as Eje Cafetero and Macizo.

ecosystemInfoModal.title: What is in the Ecosystems layer?
ecosystemInfoModal.intro: This layer comes from Colombia's official MEC ecosystem map. MEC stands for Mapa de Ecosistemas Continentales, Costeros y Marinos de Colombia: the national map of continental, coastal, and marine ecosystems.
ecosystemInfoModal.modelTitle: One polygon layer, several category labels
ecosystemInfoModal.modelCopy: A useful way to read this layer is as one national puzzle: each piece is a non-overlapping ecosystem polygon, and each polygon has several attributes. Some attributes are broad, some are detailed, and they do not always form a perfectly clean parent-child tree.
ecosystemInfoModal.valuesIntro: Expand a classification view to see the actual category values represented in the MEC layer. Area helps show ecological scale; polygon count helps show how many mapped units carry the label.
ecosystemInfoModal.mapSupportCopy: The map shows ecosystems grouped into broad biome families so the legend stays readable. The 429 unique IAvH biome-region conservation features listed below are the detailed units used by the metric source (derived from 430 authoritative raster biome IDs); the other groupings are included here for reference.
ecosystemInfoModal.valuesLoading: Loading classification values from the ecosystem layer metadata...
ecosystemInfoModal.valuesError: Classification values could not be loaded. The explanation and source links are still available.
ecosystemInfoModal.sourcesCopy: IDEAM is Colombia's Instituto de Hidrología, Meteorología y Estudios Ambientales, the public environmental information institute that publishes the MEC map. Humboldt/IAvH refers to Instituto Humboldt, Colombia's biodiversity research institute; its biome-region classification appears in the ecosystem attributes.

mapLayersPanel.speciesNote: Species layers include Humboldt BioModelos for mammals, birds, amphibians, reptiles, and plants. Fish species are shown as excluded because the available freshwater fish data is too coarse for prioritization.
mapLayersPanel.solutionNote: Distributions shown are the non-fish Humboldt BioModelos species included in this solution's calculation. Drill down to individual species when the solution includes species-level rasters.
